candidates.decision_relevance: Would let reviewers reconstruct intraday ordering and compare rebounds, drawdowns, relative performance, breadth and flow observations using only information available at each historical cutoff; this addresses repeated sequence and hindsight-leakage limitations.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W37–W45 repeatedly lack underlying hourly paths, common timestamps and freeze-time sequences; daily reviews also note asynchronous observations and post-cutoff data.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamp-aligned BTC, ETH and ETH/BTC hourly observations with contemporaneous signal snapshots
candidates.missing_history_problem: Weekly aggregates and endpoint summaries cannot establish when weakness, rebounds or other cited conditions occurred relative to one another or to analysis issuance.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would provide a consistent historical participation record for testing whether breadth deterioration or recovery persisted and how it related in time to price and relative leadership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Reviews W37–W45 and daily outputs repeatedly describe missing quantitative breadth sequences, proxy-only readings, changing constituent membership or absent methodology.
candidates.metric_name: Point-in-time constituent breadth counts and returns with universe and membership metadata
candidates.missing_history_problem: Sparse snapshots and changing proxy universes cannot distinguish durable participation changes from endpoint variation or membership effects.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would allow historical assessment of liquidation and leverage observations against price paths, while exposing source completeness and observation timing rather than relying on fragile, lower-bound snapshots.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily reviews on 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 state that liquidation aggregates are lower bounds from a fragile legacy source with unverified completeness and unreliable backfill.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped liquidation and open-interest observations with coverage/completeness metadata
candidates.missing_history_problem: Current and partial aggregates cannot establish persistence, sequence, or whether leverage observations preceded or followed price weakness.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would make it possible to evaluate persistence and divergence in settled BTC and ETH flows across the weeks under review, without treating a single session or stale weekly row as current evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W40–W45 and daily outputs repeatedly identify missing same-week settled-flow rows or only one settled session, with older rows not aligned to the reviewed period.
candidates.metric_name: Daily settled BTC and ETH ETF flow series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Isolated sessions and stale flow summaries do not show whether demand or outflows persisted or how they sequenced with price and participation.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would make the reported scorecard counts auditable at the candidate level, allowing retrospective comparison of frozen forecasts with eligible matured outcomes and separation of unavailable records from actual results.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W39–W45 repeatedly report unavailable scorecards or matured-outcome counts without candidate-linked rows, bounds and outcomes.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen forecast candidate specifications linked to maturity-eligible realized outcomes
candidates.missing_history_problem: Aggregate outcome counts cannot support verification of candidate accuracy, range containment, timing or false-positive and false-negative descriptions.
